a.onclick: openModal( this, "PEG-Lipid ~ 1.5%", ["34394960"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34394960"], ["PEG-lipids constitute the smallest fraction of the formulation - typically ~1.5-2 mol%. They create a hydrophilic steric corona around the LNP that prevents aggregation during formulation. DMG-PEG 2000 (1,2-dimyristoyl-rac-glycero-3-methoxypolyethylene glycol-2000) carries two saturated C14 (myristoyl) chains linked via a glycerol backbone to a ~2 kDa PEG chain. ALC-0159 (N,N-dimyristyl 2-hydroxyacetamide O-pegylated, ~2 kDa PEG, ~45-46 ethylene oxide units) is a non-ionic surfactant PEG-lipid used in BNT162b2."])

openModal( this, "LNP formulation", ["37747354","40927763"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37747354","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40927763"], ["The standard formulation process exploits nanoprecipitation/solvent-displacement: lipids dissolved in ethanol (organic phase) are rapidly mixed with mRNA dissolved in an acidic aqueous buffer (typically 10-100 mM sodium acetate or citrate, pH 4.0-5.0). At acidic pH, the ionizable lipid's amine is fully protonated, enabling strong electrostatic complexation with the negatively charged mRNA phosphate backbone. The drop in solvent polarity during mixing triggers spontaneous self-assembly into ~80-150 nm particles with a solid lipid core. The standard aqueous:organic volumetric ratio is 3:1, and the ionizable lipid N/P ratio (amine nitrogens to RNA phosphates) is typically set to ~6 for mRNA. After particle formation, buffer exchange by dialysis or ultrafiltration raises pH to 7.4, neutralizes the ionizable lipid, and removes ethanol.","The formulation of mRNA-LNP can be carried out with different techniques, including pipette mixing, vortex, thin-film hydration, ethanol injection, microfluidics, and impingement jet mixing (IJM)."])

openModal( this, "Phospholipids ~ 10%", ["34394960"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34394960"], ["Phospholipids (helper lipids) are the structural lipids present at ~9-10 mol% in canonical LNP formulations. The two most commonly used helper lipids are DSPC and DOPE. DSPC (1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) is a saturated phosphatidylcholine bearing two C18:0 (stearoyl) tails esterified to a glycerophosphocholine backbone. DOPE (1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine) carries two unsaturated C18:1 (oleoyl) tails and a phosphoethanolamine headgroup."])

openModal( this, "Ionizable lipid ~45%", ["34394960","42264921"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34394960","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42264921"], ["Ionizable lipids are the functional core of LNPs, typically comprising ~46-50 mol% of the total lipid mixture. Their defining feature is a tertiary amine headgroup that is protonated (positively charged) at acidic pH and neutral at physiological pH: this property drives both RNA encapsulation during formulation and endosomal escape after cellular uptake. Two clinically used ionizable lipids, developed for the COVID-19 vaccines, are ALC-0315 and SM-102. Both are ionizable tertiary amine lipids with ester-linked branched tails, but they differ in their headgroup architecture and tail geometry. ALC-0315 has a symmetric structure: a central nitrogen bearing a short 4-hydroxybutyl chain and two identical C6 linker arms each terminating in a branched 2-hexyldecanoyl ester tail (C₄₈H₉₅NO₅). SM-102 is asymmetric: its nitrogen connects one octanoyl arm (C8) ending in a branched heptadecanyl ester and one longer hexyl arm (C6) terminating in an undecyloxy-hexanoate ester, giving it an overall more unsymmetrical, single-tailed appearance compared to the twin-armed ALC-0315.","The ionizable lipid chemical structure drives RNA encapsulation and endosomal escape. Importantly, the choice of ionizable lipids are not necessarily mutually exclusive: some novel LNP formulations aim at including both."])

openModal( this, "Cholesterol ~ 40%", ["34394960"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34394960"], ["Cholesterol - the same molecule found in mammalian cell membranes - is the second-largest component by mole fraction, typically at ~38.5-43 mol%. During formulation, cholesterol helps form ordered lipid raft-like microdomains within the LNP that stabilize the nanoparticle structure during self-assembly."])

openModal( this, "Bilayer stability", ["35787388"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35787388"], ["In LNPs, helper lipids are usually phospolipids that spontaneously form stable bilayers because their headgroup area matches their tail cross‑section.They sit mainly at the periphery, stabilizing the outer shell, reducing fusion/rupture and providing a more cell‑membrane‑like surface."])

openModalLink( this, "Keep small size", ["23344179"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23344179"], [["For formulation design, the PEG-lipid mol% is the single most sensitive lever for particle size control and must be held very tightly - even a 0.2-0.3 mol% deviation can shift mean diameter by 20-40 nm or cause aggregation.","https://www.cell.com/cms/10.1038/mtna.2012.28/asset/38a3bec7-92a7-4653-9065-02ff92a511e7/main.assets/gr5_lrg.jpg","Cryo-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) micrographs of lipid nanoparticle (LNP) small interfering RNA (siRNA) systems containing (a) 1 and (b) 5 mol% PEG-c-DMA."]])

openModal( this, "pH ~ 7.4", ["35787388"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35787388"], ["At formulation pH (~4) the lipid is cationic and electrostatically condenses the anionic mRNA. At physiological pH (7.4) it's essentially neutral, minimizing opsonization, nonspecific binding, and toxicity."])

openModal( this, "Neutral charge", ["34394960"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34394960"], ["The ionizable lipid is the functional core of a LNP, and its defining feature is that it changes charge depending on the surrounding pH. It has a pKa in the mildly acidic range (roughly 6–7), so at the acidic pH used during formulation it is positively charged and electrostatically binds the negatively charged mRNA, driving efficient encapsulation. Cationic/ionizable lipids are required to form electrostatic interactions with negatively charged mRNA, facilitating its encapsulation. At the physiological pH of the bloodstream (7.4), however, it becomes essentially neutral, which lowers toxicity and prolongs circulation compared with permanently cationic lipids."])

openModal( this, "Manages structure fluidity and rigidity", ["35787388"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35787388"], ["Cholesterol modulates membrane fluidity by intercalating between phospholipid tails. In particular, cholesterol inserts between the acyl chains with its rigid steroid ring aligned roughly parallel to the chains and its small OH close to the headgroup region. Cholesterol confers higher structural stability of the particle in circulation, and better membrane integrity during shear stress, mixing, freeze-thaw, and contact with serum proteins."])

openModal( this, "Fenestrated endothelium (100-200 nm)", ["40104152"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40104152"], ["The liver sinusoids are lined not by continuous endothelium but by liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) perforated with open pores, or fenestrae. These fenestrae are roughly 100-140 nm across, which places a typical ~80-100 nm LNP within the size window that can physically pass out of the sinusoidal lumen, cross the LSEC layer, and enter the space of Disse - the perisinusoidal gap where hepatocytes sit. This anatomical sieving is a major reason hepatocytes are even accessible to circulating LNPs, whereas continuous endothelium in most other tissues excludes particles of this size."])

openModal( this, "Blood flow receives 25% of cardiac output", ["40104152"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40104152"], ["The liver receives on the order of a quarter of resting cardiac output through its dual blood supply -the portal vein (draining the gut) plus the hepatic artery -giving it one of the highest perfusion rates of any organ. For an intravenously injected LNP, this means a large fraction of every circulatory pass is routed through the sinusoids, so the particles encounter the fenestrated endothelium and ApoE-primed hepatocyte surface far more often than they encounter most other tissues. High perfusion also slows transit through the wide, low-flow sinusoids, extending the dwell time available for extravasation and receptor engagement. Anatomy and receptor biology set up the trap; sheer blood flow keeps feeding particles into it."])

openModal( this, "Hepatocytes", ["41316820"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41316820"], ["For standard, IV-injected mRNA-LNPs, the hepatocytes, together with haptic phagocytes (Kuppfer cells) are the natural target. For this reason, raising the dose drives up local exposure to the ionizable lipid and to the delivered nucleic acid faster in the liver than anywhere else. At high loads this can exceed the hepatocytes' capacity to tolerate and metabolize the lipid components, producing hepatocellular stress and death that shows up clinically as transient elevations in serum transaminases (ALT/AST). In parallel, Kupffer-cell uptake and recognition of the LNP/RNA cargo can activate innate immune and inflammatory signaling, amplifying hepatic injury. The effect is characteristically dose-dependent, which is why hepatotoxicity -rather than target-organ pharmacology -is frequently the dose-limiting toxicity for systemically administered LNPs, and why lowering dose, improving lipid biodegradability, or redirecting particles away from the liver are the usual mitigation strategies."])

openModal( this, "Facilitate membrane fusion with target cells", ["35787388"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35787388"], ["The structural role of helper lipids is central for endosomal escape efficiency. DSPC, the most used phospholipid in clinical settings, high melting temperature (~55 °C) and cylindrical molecular geometry promote tightly packed, stable bilayer formation. DOPE, instead, has a cone-shaped geometry making it particularly effective at destabilizing endosomal membranes and facilitating cargo release into the cytosol."])

Importantly, the majority of these therapies are inhaled."])

openModal( this, "Kidney", ["38560369"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38560369"], ["Kidney targeting is the least clinically advanced, with most of the therapies focusing on siRNA/ASO delivery."])

openModal( this, "Muscles", ["34880218"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34880218"], ["Muscles are clinically validated for vaccines, but in this case they act more as an injection depot. Instead, there are currently preclinical efforts ongoing to treat muscular dystrophy and myopathy."])

openModal( this, "Brain", ["42060243"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42060243"], ["Brain targeting is particularly hard to achieve, because LNPs must cross the Blood Brain Barrier (BBB). Two dominant strategies: intranasal (nose-to-brain, bypassing the BBB) and engineered BBB-crossing LNPs. Studies are focusing on brain cancer and neuroinflammation."])
openModal( this, "Liver", ["38570682"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38570682"], ["Liver targeting is the most mature area, mostly protein replacement therapies."])

openModal( this, "LDLR receptors", ["40104152"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40104152"], ["Once in the bloodstream, LNPs rapidly adsorb serum proteins -most importantly apolipoprotein E (ApoE) -onto their surface, forming a protein corona. ApoE is a natural ligand for the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) family, which hepatocytes express at high density because their physiological job includes clearing ApoE-bearing lipoproteins from blood. The LNP effectively disguises itself as an endogenous lipoprotein: ApoE on its surface engages hepatocyte LDLRs and triggers receptor-mediated endocytosis. This is why ApoE is often described as essential for hepatocyte targeting: LNPs that fail to bind it lose much of their functional liver delivery even if they physically reach the hepatocyte surface."])

openModal( this, "Size and PDI", ["37747354"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37747354"], ["Size here means the hydrodynamic diameter: the particle plus its associated solvation/PEG layer as it diffuses.PDI is the width of the size distribution, derived from the cumulants fit of the Dynamic LIght Scattering (DLS) autocorrelation function (essentially the normalized variance of that distribution). PDI < 0.2 indicates a reasonably monodisperse population; < 0.1 is near-monodisperse. High PDI signals heterogeneity or aggregation and undermines batch reproducibility."])

openModal( this, "pKa (apparent, of the ionizable lipid)", ["37747354"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37747354"], ["The ionizable lipid is protonatable, so its net charge is pH-dependent. The apparent pKa is the pH at which the particle surface is 50% ionized - and it's what makes the whole delivery mechanism work across three pH environments. An apparent pKa of ~6.2-6.5 optimizes the trade-off between neutrality in blood and protonation in the endosome, and correlates with in vivo potency. It's determined by the TNS assay: TNS fluoresces on binding cationic surfaces, so titrating LNPs across pH gives a sigmoid whose inflection point is the apparent pKa."])

openModal( this, "Zeta potential", ["37747354"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37747354"], ["ζ is the electrostatic potential at the slipping plane - the boundary between the ions moving with the particle and the bulk dispersant within the electrical double layer. It's a proxy for effective surface charge, not the true surface potential. Its two roles: colloidal stability and biointerface behavior. Large |ζ| gives strong interparticle repulsion (DLVO), resisting aggregation; near-zero ζ risks coalescence. But for LNPs at pH 7.4 you deliberately want a near-neutral to slightly negative value (~±10 mV), because PEGylation plus the uncharged ionizable lipid suppress protein-corona formation and premature clearance. So it's a designed compromise, not a maximization. Measured by electrophoretic light scattering (laser Doppler electrophoresis): electrophoretic mobility under an applied field is converted to ζ via Henry/Smoluchowski. Ionic strength matters -always report the buffer, since ζ collapses at high salt."])

openModal( this, "Encapsulation efficiency", ["37747354"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37747354"], ["EE quantifies the fraction of input mRNA sequestered within the lipid core versus free in solution. Free mRNA is rapidly degraded by serum RNases and doesn't traffic into cells, so EE is a direct determinant of potency and dose accuracy. Well-formulated LNPs typically reach ≥90%. Measured via RiboGreen, exploiting membrane impermeability of the dye: one reading without detergent quantifies only accessible (external/free) RNA; a second after Triton X-100 lysis quantifies total RNA. EncapsulationEfficiency = (total − free)/total. The total signal also gives recovered mRNA concentration, allowing to back-calculate against the input and the N/P ratio used."])

openModal( this, "RNA integrity", ["37747354"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37747354"], ["Formulation subjects mRNA to shear, low pH, and organic solvent, any of which can cleave the strand. The mRNA is extracted (e.g., phenol-chloroform or column, after LNP disruption) and resolved by denaturing agarose electrophoresis or, better, capillary electrophoresis (Bioanalyzer/TapeStation/Fragment Analyzer). Intact mRNA appears as a single band/electropherogram peak at the expected nucleotide length; degradation manifests as smearing or a low-molecular-weight shoulder. CE gives a quantitative % intact metric rather than a qualitative gel readout."])

openModal( this, "Targeting moieties bound to PEG lipids", ["36691401"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36691401"], ["A standard four-component LNP has an intrinsic tropism dominated by the liver, because in circulation it adsorbs apolipoprotein E and is captured by hepatocyte LDL-family receptors. This tropism can first be steered \"passively\" by tuning the same lipid components - swapping the ionizable lipid, adjusting molar ratios, or adding different charged lipids shifts accumulation toward lung, spleen, and other tissues. Active targeting adds a further layer on top of this: a ligand (antibody, sugar, aptamer, or peptide) is conjugated to the distal terminus of the PEG-lipid so that it projects beyond the PEG corona and engages a specific cell-surface receptor, promoting receptor-mediated binding and endocytosis and redirecting the particle to a chosen cell population rather than to the default hepatic route."])

openModal( this, "Endosomal Escape", ["40629129","23799535"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40629129","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23799535"], ["The HII-phase transitions rupture the endosomal membrane and release cargo into the cytosol - the basis of endosomal escape. The process is strikingly inefficient, though: usually only ~1-10% of internalized mRNA reaches the cytoplasm, a central bottleneck for LNP potency. ","Biodegradability then governs the components' fate: cholesterol and phospholipid are endogenously metabolized and the PEG-lipid desorbs and clears, but the synthetic ionizable lipid is the main toxicological concern because it can accumulate. Modern ionizable lipids therefore carry biodegradable ester bonds — stable at physiological pH but enzymatically hydrolyzed in tissues into smaller, hydrophilic fragments that are readily excreted, improving tolerability and enabling repeat dosing."])

openModal( this, "Endosome pH acidification", ["40629129"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40629129"], ["As the endosome acidifies, the ionizable lipid re-protonates and pairs electrostatically with anionic endosomal phospholipids. These ion pairs adopt a cone shape (bulky tail, small headgroup) incompatible with a flat bilayer, driving negative curvature and a lamellar-to-inverted-hexagonal (HII) transition that destabilizes the membrane. This is why lipid shape matters: cone-shaped lipids (favored by protonation and by unsaturated or branched tails) promote this rupture-prone geometry, whereas cylindrical lipids like the saturated helper DSPC pack into stable bilayers - good for particle structure, poor at breaking membranes. The ionizable lipids themselves (e.g. SM-102, ALC-0315) are non-lamellar amino lipids whose wedge-shaped tails do not form stable bilayers."])

openModal( this, "Anti-PECAM-1 (CD31)", ["30336167"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30336167"], ["PECAM-1/CD31 is constitutively and abundantly expressed at endothelial junctions, and the pulmonary vasculature offers the largest accessible endothelial surface to an intravenous bolus. Antibody-decorated LNPs bind luminal PECAM-1 on the first vascular bed encountered (the lungs), anchoring the particle to endothelium and driving its uptake there. Conjugating mRNA-LNPs with anti-PECAM-1 antibodies profoundly inhibits hepatic uptake while raising pulmonary mRNA delivery ~200-fold, and this re-targeting is independent of apolipoprotein E - i.e. it works through receptor engagement rather than the endogenous ApoE pathway."])

openModal( this, "Anti-Transferrin Receptor (TfR)", ["31376426"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31376426"], ["The transferrin receptor is enriched on the luminal membrane of brain capillary endothelial cells, making it the most-used handle for crossing the blood–brain barrier. An anti-TfR antibody engages the receptor and co-opts its transcytosis pathway to move the particle from blood across the endothelium toward the parenchyma; binding affinity is a critical tuning parameter, since excessively high affinity tends to trap the carrier in the endothelium instead of releasing it on the brain side"])

openModal( this, "Anti-CD5", ["34990237"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34990237"], ["CD5 is a pan-T-cell surface marker. openModal( this, "GalNAc", ["29792572"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29792572"], ["GalNAc is the ligand for the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR), which is expressed almost exclusively on hepatocytes, at very high copy number, and recycles quickly. Tris-GalNAc binds ASGPR, which is highly expressed on hepatocytes, resulting in rapid endocytosis and delivery of cargo into the cell. The combination of high receptor density and fast turnover is what makes this a uniquely efficient hepatocyte-targeting route; the receptor then recycles to the surface for repeated rounds of uptake."])

openModal( this, "Mannose", ["11899091"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11899091"], ["Mannosylation targets the mannose receptor (CD206), a C-type lectin. Because these are professional antigen-presenting cells, mannose-decorated carriers are internalized by APCs and channelled toward antigen-processing compartments, which is the basis for using them to boost delivery of vaccine antigens/mRNA into the cells that prime immune responses."])

openModal( this, "Transferrin", ["31376426"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31376426"], ["Here the endogenous ligand itself is used: iron-loaded transferrin binds TfR on brain capillary endothelium and is internalized and transcytosed via the receptor's natural trafficking cycle, carrying the LNP toward the brain. Among the many potential blood–brain-barrier targets, the transferrin receptor expressed by brain capillary endothelial cells remains the most common target for brain delivery. A practical limitation of the natural-ligand approach is competition with the high concentration of endogenous transferrin already circulating for the same binding site."])

openModal( this, "A10 (A10-3.2)", ["19701187"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19701187"], ["PSMA is a membrane antigen strongly overexpressed on prostate cancer cells. openModal( this, "Gint4.T", ["24566984"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24566984"], ["PDGFRβ is a receptor tyrosine kinase overexpressed in glioblastoma. openModal( this, "AS1411", ["37808518"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37808518"], ["Nucleolin is normally nucleolar but is aberrantly displayed on the surface of many tumor cells (and tumor vasculature) while largely absent from normal cell surfaces. AS1411 is a guanosine-rich aptamer that binds nucleolin, is internalized in tumor cells, and localizes to cells overexpressing nucleolin. Uptake is driven by nucleolin's shuttling/macropinocytosis, delivering cargo intracellularly; distinctively, AS1411 also exerts an intrinsic antiproliferative effect by interfering with nucleolin function, so the moiety is not purely a delivery handle."])

openModal( this, "Stealth effect", ["37162501","32827675"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37162501","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32827675"], ["PEG-lipids confer a stealth effect on LNPs by forming a dense hydrophilic corona: the flexible polyethylene glycol chains project outward into the aqueous phase and adopt a mushroom-like conformation at the ~1.5-2 mol% densities typical in mRNA-LNP formulations, generating an entropic repulsive force that prevents macromolecules from approaching the lipid surface.","PEGylation renders the LNP surface unrecognizable to the Fcγ and complement receptors of circulating monocytes and resident macrophages of the mononuclear phagocyte system, substantially extending circulatory half-life. openModal( this, "Cholesteryl succinate", ["41235139"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41235139"], ["Finally, functionalized sterols such as cholesteryl succinate introduce charged or ionizable groups onto the sterol scaffold, modifying surface charge, protein corona composition and receptor interactions; these derivatives can promote more localized retention and cell-type-specific uptake -for example at the injection site or in particular vascular beds -shifting the overall biodistribution and organ tropism compared with standard cholesterol-based LNPs."])

openModal( this, "Sitosterol", ["35889670"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35889670"], ["In contrast, plant-derived sterols such as β-sitosterol drive the formation of more faceted, polymorphic and multilamellar particles, which alters protein corona composition, endosomal escape efficiency and uptake routes, frequently reducing the default liver bias and enabling enhanced transfection in extrahepatic tissues including immune cells and macrophages."])

openModal( this, "20-Hydroxy cholesterol", ["35569584"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35569584"], ["Oxysterols such as 20-hydroxycholesterol represent a distinct class of modified sterols: by disrupting endosomal recycling pathways, they increase late-endosome retention of LNPs and thereby improve mRNA delivery to cell types that are otherwise resistant to transfection, such as primary T cells and other immune populations."])

openModalLink( this, "Protein Corona", ["42285973"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42285973"], [["As the PEG-lipids shed, they increasingly leave the LNP surface available for plasma proteins to bind. The protein corona is a dynamic element that changes with time and which identity is strongly based on LNP characteristics, especially apparent pKa. One of the most advanced techniques to visualize the 3D structure of the protein corona is cryo-electron microscopy, combined with cryo-electron tomography. However, while this technology clearly reveals the formation of protein corona on hard, polystyrene nanoparticles, it is not as visible in LNPs or endogenous extracellular vesicles. Protein corona formation is a dynamic process, and protein signature is time and environment dependent.","https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-74240-4/figures/4","Cryo-TEM image capturing polystyrene nanoparticles and lipid nanoparticles. openModal( this, "Apparent pKa", ["35787388"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35787388"], ["The apparent pKa of ionizable lipids determines how much positive charge the LNP presents as it traverses pH gradients (blood, interstitium, endosomes), and this strongly affects which cells and tissues it interacts with."])

openModal( this, "Neutral", ["35787388"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35787388"], ["Clinically validated mRNA LNPs such as those based on ALC‑0315 (Comirnaty) or SM‑102 (Spikevax), typically combined with DSPC, cholesterol and a PEG-lipid, are designed so that the ionizable lipid is largely neutral at pH 7.4 and becomes protonated only when exposed to endosomal pH. The helper phospholipid (often DSPC, sometimes DOPE or similar PCs/PEs) is zwitterionic and effectively neutral at physiological pH, so the formulation overall has low surface charge in circulation."])

openModal( this, "Anionic", ["35346768"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35346768"], ["Formulations that are net anionic or more negatively charged at physiological pH, usually are achieved by incorporating anionic helper phospholipids (e.g. DOPS, DOPG). They tend to redistribute away from hepatocytes and toward spleen and other elements of the mononuclear phagocyte system. Anionic helper lipids increase the negative surface charge and promote recognition and uptake by splenic macrophages, dendritic cells, and other antigen-presenting cells enriched in the marginal zone and red pulp, where scavenger receptors and proteoglycans preferentially bind anionic surfaces. These formulations are attractive when the goal is systemic immunomodulation or vaccination with strong splenic APC engagement."])

openModal( this, "Cationic", ["35346768"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35346768"], ["Cationic or more strongly protonated LNPs at physiological pH tend to show enhanced uptake in the lung, especially when administered systemically at doses where plasma-exposed endothelium is a major interface. When the apparent pKa is shifted upward (permanent cationic lipids are used), a significant positive charge is present at pH 7.4, leading to strong electrostatic interactions with the highly glycosaminoglycan-rich pulmonary endothelium and capillary network, as well as with anionic components of the alveolar surface when delivered intravascularly or intratracheally. This can be achieved with “classic” permanently cationic lipids (e.g. DOTAP-like). Mechanistically, the lung bias is often rationalized as a combination of: (i) stronger binding to endothelial proteoglycans in the lung, (ii) mechanical trapping of slightly larger or stickier particles in the dense pulmonary capillary bed, and (iii) efficient endosomal escape boosted by pre-existing cationic character."])
